gimbalPad.slewTip: Drag to slew gimbal · release to stop

health.framesDropped: {{n}} frames dropped: this machine is behind
health.lossHigh: {{pct}}% packet loss: check the radio link

panel.copyDiagnosticsHint: Binary paths, versions, hub and ffmpeg logs, for a bug report.
panel.linkStatsHint: Bitrate, framerate, packet loss and dropped frames over the feed.
panel.lockTip: Lock this panel to the current vehicle
panel.lockedTip: Locked to this vehicle, click to follow active
panel.noFeedConfigured: No feed configured for {{vehicle}}.<add>Add a feed</add><muted>or switch to</muted><mode>Synthetic</mode>.
panel.noFeeds: No feeds configured. Open Sources to add one per vehicle.
panel.noVehicle: No vehicle selected. Connect or select a vehicle to view its feed.
panel.overlaysTip: Overlays: OSD layers, link stats, terrain
panel.qualityHighTip: Most elevation detail, heaviest to load
panel.qualityLowTip: Fewer elevation samples, lightest on the GPU
panel.syntheticTip: Synthetic vision (3D terrain from GPS + attitude)
panel.terrainHint: The ground nearest the aircraft always uses the sharpest imagery.

ardudeckSim.label: ArduDeck Simulator (FPV feed)
ardudeckSim.note: Tick "Stream FPV to ArduDeck" in the simulator launcher. Swap in the simulator machine's address if it runs elsewhere. Port 8654 is the simulator's own media hub, kept clear of this one's 8554.

herelink.label: Herelink (ground unit)
herelink.note: WiFi hotspot mode. USB-tether uses 192.168.42.129; station mode uses the assigned IP.

mavlink.label: Advertised by vehicle (MAVLink)
mavlink.note: Auto-discovers the stream URI from VIDEO_STREAM_INFORMATION. Falls back to manual if the vehicle never advertises one.

rtpUdp.label: Custom RTP / UDP (H.264)
rtpUdp.note: Raw H.264 over UDP, e.g. a companion-computer GStreamer pipeline.

rtsp.label: Custom RTSP URL
rtsp.note: Any RTSP source. The hub republishes it as low-latency WebRTC.

rubyfpv.label: RubyFPV (relayed video)
rubyfpv.note: Enable "video forwarding to local network" in RubyFPV. The engine bridges its raw H.264/UDP into the hub.

siyiA8.label: SIYI A8 mini / ZR10 / ZR30
siyiA8.note: Camera + autopilot must share the 192.168.144.x subnet. Set the IP in SIYI Assistant.

srt.label: Custom SRT
srt.note: Higher latency than RTP but resilient over lossy long-haul links.

uvc.label: USB / HDMI capture device
uvc.note: Analog-FPV-to-USB dongle or capture card on this machine. Played locally: the only path suitable for piloting.

webrtc.label: Custom WebRTC (WHEP)
webrtc.note: A WHEP endpoint published by a companion computer. Lowest latency, played directly.

settings.bitrateHint: Higher looks better but needs a cleaner link. Changes without interrupting the picture.
settings.codecH264Hint: Plays in ArduDeck as it arrives, without conversion.
settings.codecH265Hint: More detail for the same bitrate. ArduDeck converts it for display, which costs a little latency.
settings.didNotStick: {{names}} did not stick. The camera kept its own value.
settings.effectLinkRestart: link restarts for a few seconds
settings.fixedAddress: Give that adapter the fixed address 192.168.1.20, mask 255.255.255.0, then press Find again.
settings.groundMustMove: The ground receiver has to move to channel {{channel}} too.
settings.ipv4StepsMac: System Settings, Network, the adapter, Details, TCP/IP: Configure IPv4 Manually.
settings.ipv4StepsWindows: Settings, Network & internet, Ethernet, IP assignment, Edit: Manual, IPv4 on.
settings.ldpcHint: Stronger error correction. The ground adapter has to support it; RunCam ships it off.
settings.loginRejected: Found a camera at <host>{{host}}</host>, but it turned down RunCam's default login. Enter the one you set on it.
settings.mcsHint: Lower reaches further, higher carries more data. Keep the bitrate within what the link can carry.
settings.neutralTip: Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue back to 50
settings.noAddress: The wired adapter ({{adapters}}) is connected but has no address. That is what happens with the camera plugged straight into this computer: there is no router handing addresses out.
settings.noneAnswered: No WiFiLink answered on this computer's networks. Check the camera is powered and its Ethernet lead is seated at both ends, then try again.
settings.notTaken: The camera did not take the changes.
settings.oldFirmware: This firmware is older than ArduDeck can write to safely. The values are shown as the camera reports them; update the camera to V3.1 or newer to change them here.
settings.orientationHint: For a camera mounted upside down or sideways.
settings.pickOne: More than one camera answered. Pick yours:
settings.pictureNote: The picture reloads for a moment when these are applied, so you see the result in the feed.
settings.plugIn: Plug the camera's Ethernet lead (the 4-pin adapter in the box) into this computer or your router and power the camera. These are its own settings, changed over that cable, not over the video link.
settings.powerHint: More power runs the unit hotter (give it airflow) and may be more than is allowed where you fly. RunCam applies power as the link restarts, and the camera can reboot.
settings.quarterTurn: A quarter turn stands the picture on its side.
settings.savedLinkRestart: Saved. The video link is restarting; the picture returns in a few seconds.
settings.savedPower: Saved. RunCam applies the new power as the link restarts, which can reboot the camera.
settings.sdRecordingHint: Records the camera's own video to its SD card, independent of this computer.
settings.sdSettingsFile: The camera has a settings file on its SD card, which RunCam re-applies every time it starts. ArduDeck updates that file as well, so your changes survive a restart.
settings.sensorLimitTip: This sensor runs 1080p at up to 90 fps
settings.showingCurrent: Showing what the camera holds now.
settings.stbcHint: Sturdier reception on a ground adapter with two antennas. RunCam ships it off.
settings.switchReceiver: Switch this computer's receiver to {{channel}} as well
settings.telemetryMavlinkHint: Forwards the flight controller's MAVLink over the link, so ArduDeck can connect through it.
settings.telemetryMspHint: Draws the flight controller's OSD onto the picture from MSP.
settings.videoLinkNote: The ground side has to use the same channel and pairing key, or the picture stops until it does. Changes here restart the link for a few seconds.

sourceMenu.cameraSettingsTip: Resolution, bitrate, picture and radio settings on the camera itself
sourceMenu.codecTip: Codec the camera sends. WiFiLink 2 defaults to H.265.
sourceMenu.controlTip: How the GCS commands the mount. Auto/Manager use the MAVLink gimbal manager (ArduPilot 4.1+). Mount control uses DO_MOUNT_CONTROL for legacy mounts. RC-driven = flown from the transmitter (display only). Off hides the controls.
sourceMenu.convertTip: Convert to H.264 so the stream can render (required for H.265; costs some CPU)
sourceMenu.hfovTip: Horizontal field of view, needed for click-to-point accuracy
sourceMenu.lowLatencyTip: Low-latency: small jitter buffer, drop late frames
sourceMenu.mountTip: Which mount instance to command (0 = all gimbals, 1 = MNT1, 2 = MNT2).
sourceMenu.rtspTip: RTSP transport. TCP (default) works through firewalls and lossy links. UDP has the lowest latency on a clean LAN but needs the firewall to let ArduDeck's media hub in. Auto tries UDP first.
sourceMenu.selectVehicle: Select a vehicle to configure its camera feeds.
sourceMenu.viaTip: Dongle: ArduDeck receives directly with the plugged-in dongle. Network: a separate ground station forwards video to the udp url.

stream.noVideoArrived: No video arrived. The feed connected but sent no frames.
stream.viewHidden: This view is hidden (another tab or collapsed). Show it, then start the stream.

streamPopover.cpuLimited: Encoder is CPU-limited. Untick HUD or shrink the panel to lighten it.
streamPopover.opencvHint: RTSP is served over TCP. For OpenCV, set {{env}} to skip the UDP attempt.
streamPopover.title: Video stream
streamPopover.what3d: Sends the 3D view only, without HUD or controls.
streamPopover.whatHud: Sends the followed vehicle's view with HUD and OSD, rendered on its own so nothing on screen covers it.
streamPopover.whatTerrain: Sends the terrain only, without HUD or OSD.

svt.needsFix: Synthetic vision needs a GPS fix from {{vehicle}}.
svt.terrainUnavailable: Terrain data unavailable, check the internet connection.

view.clickToPoint: Click to point gimbal at target
view.h265Keyframe: H.265 cameras need their next keyframe before the first picture
view.phaseChecking: Camera answered, checking the video is arriving…
view.stalledHint: The feed stopped delivering frames. Retrying automatically; replugging the device also recovers it.

visionStream.tip: Publish the synthetic view as a video stream for OpenCV, VLC, ffmpeg or a browser

wfbng.binaryNote: The receiver binary is on the ArduDeck releases page (build it from tools/wfb-rx to run on the PC). PixelPilot on Android can display the feed but cannot forward it.
wfbng.bwTip: Radio bandwidth - must match the VTX setting
wfbng.cannotListen: Could not listen on the port.
wfbng.channelTip: Must match the channel set on the camera VTX
wfbng.keyNote: The pairing key (gs.key) comes from the camera - created on its first boot.
wfbng.keyTip: The camera creates gs.key on its first boot - fetch it once from the camera's SD card or web interface
wfbng.nothingOnPort: Nothing on port {{port}} yet - make sure the ground station shows video and forwards to this computer's IP.
wfbng.plugDongle: Plug the WiFi dongle from the camera kit into this computer
wfbng.portBusy: Port {{port}} is busy - if the feed is already running, that is the stream itself.
wfbng.ready: Ready - press Add, select the feed, and power the camera.
wfbng.separateGs: Using a separate ground station instead?
wfbng.separateGsHint: If this computer can't power the dongle (dark LED / USB errors), run the receiver on another machine that can - a PC, or a Linux / Radxa / Raspberry Pi box - and have it forward the video here over your network. Both machines must be on the same network. Then set this feed to Network mode.
wfbng.testTip: Listens for a couple of seconds and reports what is arriving
wfbng.videoDetected: Video detected - press Add and select the feed.
wfbng.videoDetectedFrom: Video detected from {{sender}} - press Add and select the feed.
